summary.title: Making the Netflix API More Resilient
summary.one_liner: Learn how Netflix wrapped its API's service dependencies in a circuit breaker with fallbacks and a 10-second real-time stats dashboard to keep streaming up during failures.
keywords: timeouts and exceptions in remote calls
takeaways: Wrap each service dependency in a decorator that tracks call results and trips a circuit when the error rate passes a threshold.
Failures counted toward tripping include request timeouts, a full thread pool and bounded queue, and client library exceptions.
Choose a fallback per dependency: custom (cache or client fallback), fail silent (return null), or fail fast (return 5xx) when data is required.
Use a short rolling window (10 seconds here) and real-time dashboards so decisions and diagnostics reflect what is happening now.
summary.summary: This 2011 Netflix Tech Blog post by Ben Schmaus explains how the Netflix API team made its service dependency layer more resilient. It describes a circuit breaker decorator inspired by Michael Nygard's CircuitBreaker pattern, which counts failures over a 10-second rolling window and serves fallbacks when a threshold is exceeded. The post covers three fallback strategies (custom, fail silent, fail fast) and a real incident where database throttling tripped a circuit and a local query cache kept member impact low. It also shows a traffic-light style dashboard used for diagnostics.
